sentences.text: Thambetochen species were large, flightless ducks possessing robust legs and small wings.
This genus belongs to the family Anatidae, which includes modern ducks.
Fossils of T. chauliodous were found on Maui and Molokai, while T. xanion fossils were found on Oahu.
These ducks had beaks with tooth-like lamellae and a diet of plants digested via hindgut fermentation.
These ducks evolved in isolation on islands that lacked terrestrial mammals.
The genus Thambetochen was described by Olson and Wetmore in 1976.
The genus contains two species: T. chauliodous and T. xanion.
Thambetochen lived from the Gelasian to the Holocene, between 2.58 and 0 million years ago.
Thambetochen likely went extinct when Polynesians colonized the Hawaiian islands.
